the fake-gh.js comment-cloning fix is a small addition to a file not in this task's owned-paths list, but was necessary for the regression test to actually detect the bug (object-reference sharing was masking it)

results.summary: Fixed: loop() reused one ctx for every tick, and listComments memoized comments:<n> in ctx._cache with no expiry, so a run record written by another process (request-changes, a worker's finish/block) was invisible to a loop that had already read that card. Added dropCommentCaches(ctx), called at the top of tick(), which drops every comments:<n> entry (base and mergeGate stay, they're legitimately per-process). Also fixed test/fake-gh.js: its comment GET returned live object references, so the run record's in-place PATCH from a second ctx was silently visible through an array the first ctx was still holding, which masked this exact bug in a naive two-tick test; GET now returns a snapshot per call, matching a real REST response. Added a regression test in test/dispatch.test.js (verified it fails without the dispatch.js fix even with the fake-gh fix, and passes with both). Audited every other loadRun call site in tick() (reconcileClosed, the reclaim loop, the orphan lock sweep, the remaining claim-loop guards) - all read through the same ctx and get the same one-tick freshness with no further changes needed. PR: https://github.com/emyann/harness-kanban-board/pull/212
